summary: Implemented the Phase 4 task 4.6 renderer behavior matrix as test-only work with no production change. Seven new files under tests/ArrTags.Tests add 51 cases (40 unguarded, 11 environment-guarded real render cases): RendererBehaviorFixtures (synthetic repository-owned sources, metadata builders, and PNG structural parsing), RendererBehaviorDimensionTests, RendererBehaviorFormatTests, RendererBehaviorTruncationTests, RendererBehaviorLayoutTests, RendererBehaviorCancellationTests, and RendererBehaviorFailureTests. Dimensions: a pure theory proves clamp(width/1000, 0.5, 4.0) scales the ADR-009 geometry (pill height and outer inset) for widths 320/500/1000/2000/5000, and guarded renders prove a 320x480 opaque source, a 2000x3000 opaque source, a 720x480 alpha source, an EXIF orientation-3 JPEG, and an EXIF orientation-8 JPEG all keep the oriented source dimensions and IHDR dimensions with no upscaling or downscaling. Format: guarded structural parsing proves a non-interlaced 8-bit PNG, RGB (color type 2) for opaque output and RGBA (color type 6) for meaningful alpha, an sRGB chunk, an IEND terminator, and no retained iCCP/eXIf/tIME/tEXt/zTXt/iTXt source metadata; a semi-transparent source pixel keeps straight alpha (alpha 128 and RGB within one channel step), and a hand-crafted straight-alpha source with non-zero hidden RGB on a fully transparent pixel is canonicalized to #00000000. Truncation: a resolved 40-scalar custom value normalizes to a 21-scalar prefix plus '...' (24 total), a 24-scalar value is unchanged, whitespace/control scalars are normalized first, a value that cannot fit any pill is omitted without expanding lower-priority values, width fitting shortens an over-wide 24-scalar label further while staying within the 24-scalar bound, and width fitting never splits a supplementary scalar. Layout: the rail packs three pills per row across two rows, overflow moves to the next row, lower-priority candidates are omitted once both rows are full, no pill is split across rows, every pill stays inside the safe area of narrow (240x600) and short (1000x150) posters, the independent top-right UPGRADE status pill resolves only from a confirmed true value and never overlaps the rail, and the technical rail is anchored bottom-left. Cancellation: a cancelled token is observed before decode and before the ineligible-surface, metadata, source-limit, and contrast decisions, returning Failed(Cancelled) with no artifact and an unchanged source. Failure/pass-through: ineligible Series/Season surfaces, a non-matched result, missing metadata, no displayable value, and an unavailable source pass through; source-byte, source-dimension, and derived-output limit violations, low contrast, an invalid color policy, a missing font resource, unsupported source bytes, and a descriptor that does not match the decoded dimensions all return exactly one bounded Failed reason with no partial PNG and an unchanged source. The same SkiaNativeFactAttribute guard used by the task 4.8/4.9 suites is reused so the default ./build.sh test stays green with the 11 new real render cases skipped.

Guard honesty re-confirmed: ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 without the pinned sysroot on the loader path fails the 4 RendererBehaviorFormatTests cases (DllNotFoundException/TypeInitializationException on libSkiaSharp native init) rather than silently passing; skipped only when ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT != 1.

Probed actual output before writing assertions: the SkiaBadgeRenderer 3.119.4 output chunks are IHDR,sBIT,sRGB,IDAT,IDAT,IEND (so the tests assert iCCP/eXIf/tIME/tEXt/zTXt/iTXt absence rather than sBIT); a semi-transparent Unpremul source pixel round-trips as alpha 128 with RGB within one channel step; a hand-crafted straight-alpha PNG with hidden RGB (0xAB,0xCD,0xEF,0) on a fully transparent pixel renders to (0,0,0,0); a truncated PNG returns Failed(UnsupportedInput); a decoded-dimension/descriptor mismatch returns Failed(MalformedSource).

Coverage review: dimensions, format behavior, truncation, layout, cancellation, and failure/pass-through are each mapped to executing assertions; the 4.9 and 4.11 boundaries were respected (no golden baselines, no strict byte/PNG oracle, no ICC fail-closed test, no renderer configuration model, no RenderVersion/RenderOutputPolicy default changes).

Inspected git status and git diff: no production source file changed; only the seven new test files and the PLANS.md/README.md/docs/changelog.md/worker-report documentation updates; the pre-existing unstaged .opencode/agents/*.md modifications remain untouched and unstaged; no package manifest or lock file changed.
known_limitations: The renderer's later cancellation checkpoints (after decode, between layout and drawing, and before finalization) are implemented in SkiaBadgeRenderer but are not independently reachable through the public synchronous RenderAsync contract without production-only injection hooks. Only the earliest (before-decode) checkpoint and its precedence over the surface, metadata, source-limit, and contrast decisions are deterministically exercised. Adding injectable hooks would be a production/rendering change, which is out of scope for this test-only task; the limitation is recorded in the test class documentation, PLANS.md, and the changelog.

Draw-failure, encode-failure, and corrupt-font/missing-native-asset RenderResult reasons are not reachable through the public contract without test-only injection. The missing-font-resource path is covered deterministically through a bogus RenderFontIdentity resource name. The environment guard proves a missing native asset fails rather than silently passing, but it is not asserted as a specific RenderResult failure reason.

The format tests assert the behavioral/structural PNG contract (8-bit depth, RGB/RGBA color type, non-interlace, chunk presence, straight alpha, canonical transparent-pixel RGB). Pinned decoded-pixel goldens, the strict byte/PNG oracle, cross-runtime tolerance, and the malformed/unsupported ICC profile fail-closed behavior remain task 4.11.
The 11 guarded Skia tests are reported as skipped by the default ./build.sh test and pass only in the forced pinned-native run; this is the established honest guard shared with tasks 4.8 and 4.9.
